questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Directions for children
School zone ahead
Playground area ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone ahead
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs warn you that you are in or near a school zone. Watch for children and follow the posted speed limit.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. No passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back into the right lane when you can see the headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving while taking medications?

options.text: Most cold medications can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications are safe if taken at the recommended dose.
Any medication prescribed by a doctor is safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications, including over-the-counter ones, can impair your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy. You must know how your medication affects your driving ability.

questions.question: In which situation should you not point your wheels straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on a level road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: On a hill, turn your wheels so your vehicle won't roll into traffic if the brakes fail. When waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight to prevent sliding into oncoming traffic if hit from behind.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on snow or ice?

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Change speed and direction gradually.
Drive as you would on dry roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change speed and direction gradually.
questions.explanation: Make speed and direction changes slowly on snow and ice. Never use cruise control because your tires may lose contact with the road and you will lose control.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to see you.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to leave room for other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked vehicles. A person may step out or a driver may pull out without seeing you.

questions.question: When a school bus has red lights flashing, you must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is pulled in.
The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: Remain stopped until the red lights turn off, the stop arm is pulled in, and the bus begins moving.

questions.question: If you want to pass a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.
Keep your speed steady. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
Rely on the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot. Look several times before changing lanes. Watch traffic in front and beside you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction on wet roads, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to gain traction.
Press the brakes firmly to stop sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle hydroplanes (rides on water), slow down gradually and do not use the brakes. This can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.
Staring straight ahead at the road.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every two to five seconds to stay aware. Do not stare straight ahead only. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: When are collisions more likely to happen?

options.text: When all vehicles travel at the same speed.
When one lane travels faster than other lanes.
When one vehicle travels faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one vehicle travels faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen when a driver goes faster or slower than other vehicles. Speeding increases collision risk. Driving too slowly can cause rear-end collisions or force other drivers to swerve.

questions.question: If someone passes you in a no passing zone, you should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down and let them safely return to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let them safely return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Slow down so the other driver can safely return to your lane. This helps everyone avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge and slow down.
Drive to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. Drive to the right edge and stop until the vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway is ending.
A divided highway is starting.
The road ahead will be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is starting.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a divided highway is ahead. Stay to the right of the center divider.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Look around constantly.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look around constantly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in your blind spots or be missed in a quick glance. Always watch carefully for them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp turn to the right ahead.
There are sharp left and right turns ahead.
The road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you the road curves ahead. Slow down to a safe speed.

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: To let other drivers merge onto the freeway.
To give the truck time to stop.
To give other drivers space to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give the truck time to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks need more distance to stop than cars. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at the same time.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap in traffic that is large enough to safely enter. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: How do stopping distance and crash severity change with speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds cause longer stopping distances and more severe crashes. Leave more space between you and other cars as your speed increases.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Cars passing them.
Cars coming toward them.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars coming toward them.
questions.explanation: A left-turning driver must wait for oncoming cars to pass. Turn only when it is safe and oncoming traffic will not be affected.

questions.question: The light turns yellow as you approach an intersection at the speed limit. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and go through without caution.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: Yellow means the light will soon turn red. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, cross carefully.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: Motorcycles do not follow the same rules as cars.
Motorcycles can stop faster than regular vehicles.
Motorcycles brake slower than regular vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles can stop faster than regular vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop quickly. Following too closely gives you no time to react if the rider brakes or makes a mistake. Keep a safe distance.

questions.question: What should you do when passing on a two-lane road?

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check how far away oncoming cars are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how far away oncoming cars are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming cars are moving. Only pass if you are sure oncoming cars are far enough away and you have room to change lanes safely.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings (like school buses and hazmat trucks).
Watch for multiple trains.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings carefully. Cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles that must stop at crossings, like school buses and hazmat trucks.

questions.question: How do you know what traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn around and look out the back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror regularly to know where cars are behind you.

questions.question: What does interstate driving require from you?

options.text: The ability to drive safely at high speeds.
Constant alertness.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving means you must stay alert at all times and be able to handle high speeds.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.
questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up and match the traffic flow. Merge smoothly when it is safe. Do not stop on the ramp.
